title: Deriving the Identity cos(x + pi/2) = -sin x
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Use the trigonometric addition formulas to derive the identity \cos(x + \pi/2) = -\sin x.

steps.title: Apply the Cosine Addition Formula
steps.explanation: Expand cos(x + pi/2) using cos(A + B) = cos A cos B - sin A sin B with A = x and B = pi/2.
steps.why: The cosine addition formula expresses the cosine of a sum in terms of sines and cosines of the summands.

steps.title: Evaluate the Quadrantal Values at pi/2
steps.explanation: At angle pi/2, the terminal point on the unit circle is (0, 1), so cos(pi/2) = 0 and sin(pi/2) = 1.
steps.why: The positive y-axis intersects the unit circle at (0, 1).

steps.title: Simplify the Expression
steps.explanation: Substitute 0 and 1 to conclude that cos(x + pi/2) = -sin x.
steps.why: Algebraic simplification reduces 0 - sin x to -sin x.
